draft.title: Psychological skills
card: Psychological skills are mental skills that help an athlete perform. Four are confidence, motivation, arousal and concentration.
belief in your own ability to do the task. Motivation is the drive to start, keep going and put in effort.
how alert and activated the body and mind are. Each task suits a best level, and too low or too high can hurt performance.

keeping attention on the cues that matter and ignoring distractions. Imagery (picturing a skill in the mind) and self-talk (words an athlete says to themselves) are two strategies that can build these skills.
draft.remember: Mental skills can be trained, and strategies like imagery and self-talk can help performance.

a.q: Before a penalty kick, Leila pictures the ball going into the corner of the goal. Which strategy is she using?
a.why: Leila is creating a picture of the skill in her mind, which is imagery. Self-talk is tempting, but it uses words said to oneself, not a mental picture.
a.clue: She is seeing the kick, not saying words.

b.q: Sam is a netballer who tenses up and fumbles passes in finals. A coach teaches her to repeat "smooth and steady" before each pass. What does this strategy mainly aim to do?
opts: Use self-talk to settle her arousal and steady her focus
Use imagery to raise her arousal before each pass
Build her motivation by giving her a reward for passing
Remove all arousal so that she stays completely calm
b.why: Repeating a phrase is self-talk, and here it helps settle arousal that is too high and keep attention on the pass. Removing all arousal is wrong, because the card says each task has a best level, not zero.
b.clue: The coach uses words, and Sam is too tense.

b.best: Use self-talk to settle her arousal and steady her focus
